newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares mixed, slump seen bottoming out.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares mixed, slump seen bottoming out.

text.p: Latvian stock volume slipped on Thursday while demand for some leading stocks exceeded supply, a sign that the recent downturn may be running its course, dealers said.
Total turnover on Thursday slipped to 105,000 lats versus 116,000 lats and Rietumu index closed 0.70 percent lower to 178.33.

Dealers said that it did not seem that investors were switching to debt from equity in response to falling T-bill yields. Attractive share prices were the main reason behind the slowing of the downturn, they said.
"The link between T-bills and securities in Latvia's case is more a theoretical one as different financial institutions are active on the two markets," one dealer said.
"The prices of RTF, Glassfibre, Riga Shipyard and Jekabpils Sugar seem to have reached an attractive level," Viesturs Shterns, head of Unibanka's securities department, told Reuters.
Valmiera Glassfibre and Riga Shipyard were the most active in trade of 28,600 lats and 26,400 lats respectively.
Valmiera was down to 1.37 lats from 1.39 lats while Riga Shipyard rose two santimes to 1.32 lats.
On the secondary list Daugavpils Chain factory and Rigas Raugs yeast factory were in demand while other stocks were dormant.
Chain slipped one santime to 2.31 lats in 6,100 lats of trade and Raugs added 10 santimes to 3.80 lats. It traded 3,800 lats of shares.
